extracted.intended_audience: prospective predoctoral and postdoctoral applicants to NICHD NRSA (F30/F31/F32) fellowships
extracted.subtask_short: applying for NICHD NRSA F fellowships
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting Individual NRSA fellowship (F30, F31, F32) applications to the NICHD, including eligibility, purpose, reviewer expectations, and policy resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goal — candidate potential and relevance to NICHD mission
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of these programs is to support promising applicants with the potential to become productive, independent investigators in priority scientific, health-related research fields relevant to the NICHD mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should articulate the applicant's potential for developing into an independent investigator and ensure the proposed research and training align with NICHD’s priority scientific and health-related research fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship/residency eligibility (NRSA limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: NRSA fellowships are limited to U.S. citizens or permanent residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be U.S. citizens or hold permanent resident status to be eligible; check full announcement for any limited exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NICHD non-participation in F33
rubrics_metrics.description: Please Note: NICHD does not participate in the Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA for Individual Senior Fellowship (F33) program for post-doctoral research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking senior individual fellowships (F33) should be aware NICHD will not accept/participate in that mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: F30 purpose and target applicants (predoctoral dual-degree)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent F30: Supports the dissertation research stages of training in combined M.D./Ph.D. and other dual doctoral degree programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility: Predoctoral students in a formal combined dual doctoral degree program who plan to become physician-scientists and other clinician-scientists, including patient-oriented researchers, in priority fields relevant to the NICHD mission. See the full announcement for detailed eligibility criteria and institution-specific access paths (with/without NIH-funded institutional predoctoral dual-degree training programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: F31 purpose and eligibility (individual predoctoral fellowship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent F31: Supports promising doctoral candidates who will be performing dissertation research and training in priority scientific, health-related research fields relevant to the NICHD mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility: Applicants with a bachelor’s degree and currently enrolled in a Ph.D. or equivalent research degree program. With limited exceptions, students must be within the first 6 years of graduate school. Applicants should submit early enough to ensure at least 2 years of dissertation-stage research training will remain at the time of award. Prospective applicants are strongly encouraged to contact NICHD's Scientific/Research Contact to discuss relevance to NICHD priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: F32 purpose and eligibility (individual postdoctoral fellowship)
rubrics_metrics.description: F32: Supports up to 3 years of postdoctoral research training in the laboratory of an established investigator (mentor). Research training must be in priority scientific, health-related research fields relevant to the NICHD mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility: Applicants must have a doctoral degree at the time of award. Applications should identify an established mentor and a training plan consistent with NICHD priorities. Duration limited to up to 3 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship requirement for F32 (training in mentor's laboratory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research training must be in the laboratory of an established investigator (mentor) for F32 awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should clearly document the mentor's role, qualifications, and commitment to provide the proposed training environment and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and duration expectations (F31/F32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should submit applications early enough to ensure that at least 2 years of dissertation-stage research training will remain at the time of award (F31). F32 supports up to 3 years of postdoctoral research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan application submission relative to your program timeline to meet minimum remaining training time requirements; budget requested support within the allowed duration limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review assignment and criteria context
rubrics_metrics.description: F31 and F32 applications assigned to NICHD are reviewed by committees at the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) based on the scientific area covered in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should align the scientific focus of their application with appropriate CSR study sections and consult CSR rosters; ensure the application addresses standard fellowship review criteria (see Fellowship Instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of parent announcements and IC-specific requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Access the Parent F30/F31/F32 Announcements and select the 'Table of IC-Specific Information, Requirements, and Staff Contacts' link within the parent announcement to find NICHD-specific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the parent announcement and the IC-specific table for NICHD-specific application requirements, staff contacts, and any deviations from the parent policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow NIH Fellowship Instructions and NRSA policy (GPS Chapter 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: F31 and F32 applicants should use the 'Fellowship Instructions.' The NIH Grants Policy Statement (GPS) outlines policies for all grant mechanisms; NRSA fellowship policies are in Chapter 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare applications strictly according to the Fellowship Instructions and relevant NRSA/GPS policies (including stipend levels, fees, and allowable budget items). Consult the NRSA Fellowship Award Policies and Notices for current stipend, fee, and budgetary levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding components described (stipend and institutional allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: These fellowships provide a stipend for salary support and a small institutional allowance to partially offset the costs of research, tuition, and health insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget requests should reflect that the award provides stipend support and a modest institutional allowance; check current NRSA notices for exact amounts and policy on allowable uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact NICHD staff before preparing application
rubrics_metrics.description: Before preparing an application, prospective applicants are strongly encouraged to contact Dennis A. Twombly, Ph.D., Deputy Director of the Office of Extramural Policy, to discuss the relevance of the proposed research and training to NICHD's research priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early contact with NICHD staff is strongly recommended to confirm fit with institute priorities and to clarify institute-specific expectations or restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upcoming changes to application and review process (effective January 25, 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: For due dates on or after January 25, 2025: Changes are coming both for how to apply for NIH fellowships as well as how NIH will review the applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with due dates on/after this date should review the announced changes and updated instructions before preparing submissions.
